title: Google will turn school AI off, including Search, until an administrator turns it on
friendlyTitle: Google will turn school AI off, including Search, until an administrator turns it on
summary: On 3 November, Chris Phillips, Google's vice president for education, said access to Gemini, Gemini Notebook, Gemini in Classroom, and Google Search will be entirely off for K-12 student accounts until a school administrator turns them on. Google says it will share the details in the coming months, before the change rolls out. Guided Learning, which coaches a student through a problem instead of giving the answer, is available in Google Classroom from today. A Search version starts as a pilot in selected United States schools later this month. TechCrunch, citing The New York Times, reports that Phillips said Search and AI are deeply integrated, and that a school which restricts AI altogether will not have Search.
friendlySummary: On 3 November, Google's education lead said Gemini, Gemini Notebook, Gemini in Classroom, and Google Search will be fully off for school student accounts until an administrator turns them on. The accounts are for students from kindergarten through year 12. Google says it will share the details in the coming months, before the change starts. A coaching tool called Guided Learning, which asks questions instead of giving the answer, is available in Google Classroom from today. A Search version starts as a trial in selected United States schools later this month. TechCrunch, citing The New York Times, reports that Google said Search and AI are now so tied together that a school which blocks AI altogether will not have Search.
whyItMatters: If a school uses Google accounts, the next decision is not whether students can open a chatbot. It is whether Search stays available at all. Google has not published the switch list yet. Ask the administrator which products the off switch covers, and whether Guided Learning in Classroom is the tool the school actually wants on.
